A1.justification: Both readable 18-page PDFs describe the same VIGOR study, with matching methods, experiments, equations and figures. Both end with references; neither supplied PDF contains an appendix, despite mentioning supplementary related work.

before.justification: V1 reports original video-generation evaluations: Best-of-N results in Table 1, streaming-search experiments in Figures 4–5, and post-hoc alignment results in Table 2.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and adds regularization and geometry-aware sampling ablation results in Tables 3–4.

M1.justification: The reward computation, geometry-aware sampling, SFT/Flow-DPO objectives and three search procedures remain unchanged. Both auxiliary-loss terms in Equation 8 already appear in v1; v3 clarifies their description and the SFT-to-DPO staging.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same RealEstate10k/GLDv2-derived GB3DV-25k data and bidirectional and streaming video-generation tasks. The added component ablations introduce no new dataset, domain or distinct test scenario.

E2.justification: Table 4 newly evaluates Uniform, Saliency and Deep Attn sampling against default GAS. This expands component-level comparators; the main Epipolar and Reproj-Pix comparison methods remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 6.5 adds regularization-weight and sampling-parameter sweeps, with unregularized and default-GAS reference settings. Existing protocols retain Best-of-N with N=10 and streaming evaluation on 16 clips with budgets 1–16. Newly disclosed defaults do not establish changes to those existing experiments.

E4.justification: V3 adds direct tests of two central design choices previously lacking component ablations: auxiliary regularization for motion preservation and GAS selection strategy, patch size and sampling ratio. Section 6.5 and Tables 3–4 substantially extend the analysis beyond the retained search-budget study.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experiment-level repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new ablations retain point-estimate reporting, and the existing candidate-seed search information is unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and Figure 4 retain identical results. V3 adds diagnostic outcomes, including a DD delta of +0.78 at lambda=0.1 against zero regularization and -4.30 for uniform sampling relative to default GAS; these supplement the existing benchmark findings.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, losses and search-complexity statements are unchanged. Equation 4 makes the source-to-target index explicit without changing the reprojection calculation. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same claims about the geometry-based reward, GB3DV-25k and reward-guided streaming search. The shortened conclusion preserves their scientific scope.

C2.justification: Section 6.5 explicitly attributes static-motion collapse to geometry-reward bias and interprets regularization and sampling tradeoffs, extending v1's brief collapse-prevention rationale. V3 also explains the already-omitted self-selection metrics in Table 1 as avoiding self-referential comparisons.

D1.justification: V3 specifies p=4, tau=20%, lambda=0.1 and gamma=0.01; clarifies SFT-before-DPO in Table 2; and identifies official-code use for Epipolar and reproduction of VideoGPA. The project link changes from the .site domain to .com. These are documentation and access-information updates.

R1.justification: Reference 17 switches from CameraCtrl to CameraCtrl II. Most other reference changes are publication-metadata updates or renumbering, while the substantive positioning relative to Epipolar-DPO and VideoGPA remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V3 condenses sampling, evaluation and conclusion prose, corrects the alignment-heading typo and search-framework figure reference, and adds Section 6.5 and acknowledgements. The overall narrative and section order remain intact.

P2.justification: V3 adds two compact ablation tables, relocates Table 2 from page 15 to page 14 and clarifies its row labels. Figure 2's caption and surrounding layout receive limited edits; existing figures retain their visual content.

improvement.justification: V3 improves reproducibility through explicit defaults and adds useful tests of previously unablated components in Tables 3–4, while preserving the existing benchmark evidence. The gain is limited: the new analyses report only VBench deltas, omit uncertainty and leave some control settings unspecified, so they do not fully substantiate the claimed geometric-coverage advantage.
